ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and transactional counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU consolidated sanctions list, and Panamanian UAF advisories; mandatory enhanced due diligence for PEPs as defined under Law 23 of 2015, including foreign and domestic PEPs, their family members and close associates; ongoing monitoring and record retention for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — electronic name clearance service available through the official registry website at www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be submitted in Spanish or in a foreign language using Latin script. Where a non-Spanish name is used, a Spanish transliteration or Spanish-language denomination is required for official registry indexing. The statutory corporate designation 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.' must appear in the name, and the full proposed name must be clearly distinguishable from all existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A company-name applicant may file a written reconsideration petition before the Office of the Director General of the Public Registry of Panama within ten business days of receiving a formal name rejection. The petition must identify the proposed name, registration application number, enclose a certified copy of the rejection resolution, and state the legal grounds under Law 32 of 1927 and the applicable Public Registry regulations. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within two months. Alternative curative measure: a revised name without the prohibited token may be resubmitted as a new 30-day reservation without losing corporate identity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable solely to satisfy the registered address requirement where a licensed resident agent maintains statutory corporate records. It does not, however, satisfy the substantive office obligation for ISIC 3250 medical-device assembly and calibration, which requires a physical establishment with operational inventory, calibration equipment, and a qualified technical supervisor for downstream Ministry of Health licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% to 45% annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection once the corporate registration and health-sector operating license are active; the probability rises to 65% or higher where the declared commercial address is a virtual maildrop or where employee declarations to the Social Security Fund do not match the registered workplace.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Ley 32 de 1927), as amended; Articles 1-16 regarding Sociedades Anónimas; Complementary rules in the Reglamento del Registro Público; Executive Decree No. 2 of 2016 for digital filings
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas, Calificación de Sociedades
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución / Pacto Social de Sociedad Anónima
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement and no escrow account obligation; capital may be subscribed in whole or in part, and the initial paid-in amount is credited to the treasury upon issuance of shares
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by unanimous written consent of the sole incorporator, effective as of [date] in the Republic of Panama, that: (1) the subscriptions to the authorized ordinary shares of the company be, and hereby are, approved, accepted, and acknowledged, with the initial subscribers' paid-in credited to the corporate treasury as reflected in the subscription ledger; (2) the registered office be, and is, established at [address], Panama, and the resident agent, [law firm], be and is ratified as the statutory resident agent authorized to accept service of process; (3) the following persons be, and are, appointed to serve until the next annual general meeting or until successors are elected: President [name], Secretary [name], and Treasurer [name], with each authorized to execute banking documents and sign contracts within company authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas; online reservation via the Registro Público portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search with up to three alternative names to avoid conflict with existing entities; submit the reservation request through the authenticated online registry system or by notarized physical application; pay the reservation fee and retain the reservation for its statutory validity period, typically 30 days, before incorporation.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation request identifying the proposed name
Power of attorney or identification of the incorporator / law firm acting as agent
Payment receipt for the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for conflict or similarity, the applicant may re-file using the second or third alternative name; if the objection is based on protected rights, an appeal may be filed with the Director General of the Registro Público within the applicable period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Authentication of the Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de la República de Panamá or Panamanian Consul abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Escritura Pública de Constitución in Spanish, including the corporate name, purpose covering the design, assembly, calibration and sale of electronic patient monitors and medical devices, capital stock as authorized, board of directors, registered office and resident agent. Appear before the notary or consul to execute and authenticate the instrument; obtain a notarized protocol. The resident agent normally prepares the charter together with the initial board consents.
required_dossiers: Charter / pacto social and proposed bylaws
Passport, corporate due diligence and background documents of subscribers and directors
Resident agent letter of acceptance and consent to serve as registered agent
Power of attorney if incorporators act through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry raises a formal authentication issue, the instrument may be corrected by marginal note or by executing a new signature page before the same notary, preserving the original submission date where legally permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry and Tax / Municipal Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Calificación de Personas Jurídicas; thereafter Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and the Municipal Authority of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized escritura with the Public Registry, either physically at the Registro Público or electronically; the Calificador will review, approve and record the instrument against the registered company folio, issuing the Certificate of Registration. After inscription, obtain the RUC from DGI, register the employer with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS), and request the municipal Aviso de Operación for the address of the registered office.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized escritura and one certified copy
Applicable Public Registry and municipal fee payment receipts
Director and shareholder due diligence packets and financial integrity declarations
Proof of registered office address and resident agent acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Calificador issues a 'nota de reparo' or formal query, the applicant must correct the defect by marginal amendment and resubmit within the statutory cure period (commonly eight to ten business days) to maintain filing priority; if refused, the company may file a recurso de reposición or sala de apelaciones.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Kickoff and Statutory Records Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, Resident Agent and, where later filings are necessary, the Registro Público
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold or adopt by unanimous written consent the first board meeting to approve the share subscriptions, ratify the registered office and resident agent, appoint officers, adopt the corporate seal, and designate banking signatories. Prepare and maintain at the registered office the minute book, share ledger, stock certificate stubs and register of directors, and file any officer or registered agent changes with the Public Registry upon occurrence.
required_dossiers: Share subscription receipts and paid-up capital records
Corporate seal and specimen signature cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subsequent officer or registered agent appointment is rejected, the board may ratify the appointment retrospectively by a unanimous written resolution and file a notarized corrective document with the Registry without invalidating actions previously taken.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección de Empresas y Actividades Industriales
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Industrial / Licencia de Operación para Fabricación de Equipos Médicos; Municipal Aviso de Operación; Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento from the Ministerio de Salud

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Reporte de Impacto Ambiental / Descripción Ambiental; full detailed EIA (Categoría II or III) is not required for low-impact assembly and calibration operations unless the facility uses solvent-based cleaning, metal finishing or battery production processes that produce significant emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Del Ejecutivo No. 1 de 2015: pH 6-9, BOD5 no greater than 100 mg/L, TSS no greater than 100 mg/L, fats and oils no greater than 15 mg/L and temperature no greater than 40°C; VOC emissions from solvent use must be controlled by abatement equipment such as activated carbon adsorption or oxidation, maintaining boundary concentrations below applicable NIOSH/NTP occupational exposure limits; hazardous waste from discarded electronic components, lead-acid batteries and calibration chemicals must be handled, stored and disposed of through MiAMBIENTE-licensed transporters and final facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá inspection and Certificate of Fire Prevention and Safety; structural occupancy and floor-load review with the municipal architecture control office; occupational health and safety registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) and CSS employer accident insurance for all technical and assembly personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – General Revenue Directorate of the Ministry of Economy and Finance of the Republic of Panama. Operational portal: SISTEMA TAX (DGI Digital Services) at dgi.mef.gob.pa and the SIVE electronic invoicing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) beneficially owned by non-residents, the statutory TIN/RUC is procured after (1) incorporation is recorded in the Registro Público de Panamá, and (2) a Panama-licensed resident agent has been appointed. The resident agent files with the DGI an application for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), submits the corporate charter and articles of incorporation, files an 'Aviso de Operación' (business opening notice), obtains the corporate digital signature certificate, and registers the authorized invoicing system. Non-resident beneficial owners are not required to appear in person; a notarized power of attorney and passport copies are sufficient. The DGI issues a 'Certificado de Registro Único de Contribuyente' containing the RUC number used for income tax, ITBMS, and customs purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: corporate income tax is imposed only on income generated from Panamanian-source operations; foreign-source income (including revenue from offshore exports where the sale occurs abroad) is not subject to Panamanian corporate income tax. For ITBMS (indirect tax), the entity is a regular taxable person if it carries out taxable transfers, imports, or taxable services in Panama, regardless of territorial-source classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a U.S.-style 'check-the-box' or deemed pass-through entity election. Available statutory elections are limited to: (i) the simplified small-taxpayer regime (Pequeño Contribuyente) for gross annual receipts under the legal threshold; (ii) the optional calculation of ITBMS liability on the basis of input/output tax only rather than requiring monthly advances, subject to DGI approval; and (iii) elections under export incentive or free-zone laws (e.g., Ley 41 de 2007) for approved exporters. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized under the Panamanian Tax Code.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – Panamanian VAT-equivalent indirect tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No fixed general economic-turnover threshold triggers ITBMS registration; any person habitually engaging in taxable imports, transfers of movable property, or taxable services in Panama must obtain a RUC and register for ITBMS. A simplified 'small taxpayer' regime is available for businesses with gross annual receipts of up to PAB 150,000 (USD 150,000).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) under DGI regulations. Invoices must be generated through a DGI-authorized electronic invoicing system or the DGI's SIVE platform, and invoice numbering must be pre-authorized by the DGI (Certificado de Autorización de Impresión for physical/electronic ranges). Taxpayers transmit invoice XML data to the DGI through the prescribed web services using a valid digital certificate, and receive an electronic acknowledgement identifying each accepted batch. Real-time fiscal clearance applies to manufacturers and other high-volume taxpayers; for exporters, the 0% export invoices are cross-validated against the customs declaration system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods, including electronic patient monitoring equipment, are zero-rated for ITBMS purposes when such goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory, ownership passes to a non-resident buyer, and the goods are not used or consumed in Panama. Offshore services, including telemetry data processing or calibration services for foreign buyers, are zero-rated when the direct beneficiary is a non-resident and the service is effectively not consumed in Panama. The taxpayer must hold an active RUC with the relevant export activity classification and must be registered in the DGI exporter registry.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Mercancías / DUA – Declaración Única Aduanera) accepted by the Panama Customs Authority (ANA), including the Electronic Export Number (EAE)
Bill of Lading (ocean, airway, or land manifest) clearly evidencing dispatch from a Panamanian port or warehouse to a foreign destination
Commercial invoice stating the transaction value in USD and showing the applicable 0% ITBMS treatment
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) issued by a Panamanian bank demonstrating successful repatriation and deposit of export proceeds in a local bank account
Certificate of Origin and shipping/insurance documentation evidencing the physical movement of goods to the non-resident buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and the Panama Customs Authority (ANA) jointly audit export zero-rating claims by reconciling the customs export declaration, the ITBMS return, and the inward remittance certificate. If any export claim is unsupported or documents are found fraudulent, the 0% treatment is clawed back with statutory interest from the date the tax would otherwise have been due. Additional penalties include fines up to 50% of the omitted tax under Código Fiscal Article 784, criminal liability for falsifying export documentation, disqualification from future zero-rating, and, where the recipient is actually a Panamanian resident, an automatic reclassification as territorial-source taxable revenue subject to income tax and ITBMS penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no central bank issuing local currency; the United States dollar is legal tender. Banking and payment-system supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). The State-owned Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the Republic, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance supervises tax-clearance requirements relevant to outbound remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama's monetary regime is fully dollarized, so there is no local fiat currency and no foreign-exchange control authority. Capital-account and current-account convertibility are unrestricted. Profit and dividend remittances are freely transferable, but banks require the remitting entity to be in good tax standing (Paz y Salvo) and to provide the underlying corporate resolution. For outbound payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, the payer must observe Panama's tax transparency rules, which may render expenses non-deductible if the beneficiary lacks economic substance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panamanian law imposes no statutory surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no conversion ratio. The exporter may retain USD or any other convertible currency freely in SBP-regulated bank accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Forex and Liquidity Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Medium only for ancillary collection and payment passthrough. Offshore digital EMI accounts are not legally recognized as bank accounts in Panama; a foreign fintech/EMI cannot debit or credit local accounts without a license from the SBP. Panama's fintech sandbox allows supervised electronic-money institutions, but for high-value ECG equipment transactions, import LC issuances and export collections must clear through an SBP-regulated commercial bank. Any inbound funds routed to the S.A. through an unlicensed overseas EMI will likely be rejected or frozen pending enhanced due diligence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one fully authorized legal representative, normally an apoderado with general banking powers, must complete the bank's KYC interview and sign the account opening documents. In standard practice, physical attendance at the compliance officer is the default mandate; remote opening is permitted only for a non-resident beneficial owner when the local legal representative physically attends, digital identification is certified, and the bank accepts an advanced electronic signature under Panamanian law. Directors who are not authorized signatories generally need not appear, but every natural-person beneficial owner must be disclosed in the bank's beneficial ownership registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership through a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with broad discretionary language, no named beneficiaries, and no documentary trail for the distribution of medical-device assembly profits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foundation deed and foundation council resolution appointing the S.A.'s legal representative; formal beneficial ownership certificate identifying all natural persons with 10% or greater economic interest; the S.A.'s retained share registry and issued stock certificates; IFRS-compliant audited financial statements; lease or ownership proof for the assembly/calibration facility; a notarized sworn declaration that no bearer shares exist; resident agent certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian law firm; and reference letters from the bank or legal counsel confirming the flow of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border sales of ECG telemetry equipment to Latam hospital procurement bodies, ministries of health, or public purchasing agencies, particularly where high unit prices or third-party intermediaries are involved.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed hospital purchase order or procurement award; end-user undertaking; complete intermediary commission agreement; certified pro-forma invoice and final commercial invoice; import permit or health-registry clearance from the destination country; ISO 13485 quality certificate, CE marking and FDA-cleared equipment documentation; calibration and test certificates; transport and insurance documents; bank statements or SWIFT records evidencing LC proceeds; negative PEP declaration of hospital officials, intermediaries and all beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty, purchasing country, or payment corridor appearing on OFAC, EU, UN, or national restrictive lists, or use of a high-risk clearing bank in a jurisdiction with weak AML standards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions and adverse-media screening reports; OFAC/EU/UN legal opinion confirming no restricted-party exposure; full SWIFT trail routed through an SBP-regulated Panamanian bank and its United States correspondent; contractual prohibitions on transshipment or re-export to sanctioned jurisdictions; independent surveyor certificate of final destination; supplier export license and manufacturer license from the country of origin; treasury policy in line with SBP AML/CFT Resolution SBP-SRP-0004-2020; and annual client-self-declaration form.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital contributions from the foreign parent must be remitted in USD via SWIFT MT103, or via Fedwire from the parent's U.S. correspondent where applicable. The SWIFT Field 70 narrative must state 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN' to permit accurate classification by the receiving bank. The bank will require the S.A.'s board resolution authorizing the capital increase or intercompany loan, an updated shareholder register, a source-of-wealth statement for the remitter, a negative PEP declaration, and, if a loan, a signed loan agreement with market-rate interest terms. Panama has no exchange-control registration, but the receiving bank must complete internal beneficial-ownership verification before crediting the funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for component purchases and calibration supplies use USD-denominated SWIFT MT103 wire transfers or documentary letters of credit issued under UCP600. For standby and commercial LC flows, the Panamanian bank issues MT700, amendments via MT707, and settlement through MT752/MT754 with the confirming bank. USD clearing is effected through nostro accounts at New York correspondent banks via CHIPS or Fedwire; same-day local dollar clearing may use Panama's Automated Clearing House where both parties hold accounts in SBP-regulated banks. Outbound supplier payments in EUR, CNY, or other currencies require an FX conversion ticket, with the bank executing at the interbank rate plus a disclosed margin.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/EUR, USD/CNH, USD/GBP) for committed trade payables, receivables, and capital-injection timing risk.
Non-deliverable forwards on Latin American emerging-market currencies (e.g., ARS, COP, PEN) where offshore deliverability is restricted or illiquid.
Cross-currency swaps for long-term USD and multi-currency debt-service alignment, executed under an ISDA master agreement with an SBP-licensed bank or an established international counterparty.
FX swaps for short-term treasury rebalancing between USD and EUR or other freely convertible currencies, limited to operational liquidity matching.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Franchise Tax - Impuesto Anual de Personas Juridicas (asset-bracket sworn declaration and payment; base fee B/.300 for total assets up to B/.150,000; higher tiers B/.600, B/.1,500, B/.3,000 and B/.6,000 apply above the base)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas; payment via e-Tax 2.0 portal or Banco Nacional de Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three equal annual installments due 15 March, 15 June and 15 September; full single prepayment accepted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus 1% monthly compensatory interest; denial of Paz y Salvo; blocking of subsequent Registro Publico filings; registered agent resignation and administrative strike-off after prolonged arrears

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return - Declaracion Anual de Renta (Form 120) with financial statements and ITBMS reconciliation schedules attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) - e-Tax 2.0 online filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 March following the calendar-year close; within 3 months after fiscal year-end for companies authorized to use a non-calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing fine of 10% of the tax due (minimum B/.50) plus 1% per-month interest; enforced assessment, tax liens and collection proceedings for continued default; wilful non-filing referred for tax evasion prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Registry (RBF) sworn confirmation - Declaracion Anual de Beneficiarios Finales, identifying every natural person with direct or indirect 10%+ ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) - Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end (31 March for calendar-year taxpayers); any change in UBO or shareholding triggers an update within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines ranging from B/.100 up to B/.10,000 under the RBF regulation; false, incomplete or late data treated as a tax and AML compliance breach subject to aggravated sanctions and registry suspension

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Operating License Renewal - Renovacion del Aviso de Operacion (representative annual municipal tariff for a small medical-device assembly and calibration operation; tariff brackets vary with declared assets and municipality classification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipio de Panama - Tesoreria Municipal, or the municipal treasury of the district where the registered office and commercial operation sit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual payment during January; due no later than 31 January for the current operating year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal surcharge of 10% plus per-month interest; per-day late fines; suspension of the operating license; closure order for unlicensed commercial activity; failure to renew blocks issuance of municipal Paz y Salvo certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Good Standing Extract - Certificado de Persona Juridica issued by the Registro Publico, refreshed for banking, KYC, insurance and counterparty due diligence cycles
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Direccion de Certificaciones
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not a fixed statutory filing; requested on each bank/KYC annual review, within 30 days of any registered amendment, or on commercial demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No statutory delinquency applies; staleness merely deprives the certificate of evidentiary value for banking, contract execution and regulatory counterparties until a fresh extract is obtained

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial-tax model: only Panama-source income is taxed. No general statutory tax holiday exists for standard S.A.s. Preferential reductions available: (i) small-enterprise regime (Law 42/2011 as amended) applying a 10% ISR rate to corporations with annual gross revenue up to B/.200,000 (USD 200,000); (ii) free-zone regimes (Colón Free Zone, Panama Pacífico) with a reduced 5% rate on licensed export-trading/manufacturing profits; (iii) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41/2007 as amended by Law 254/2021, which may exempt foreign-source income of licensed regional headquarters subject to Economic Substance Regulations. No patent box or R&D super-deduction exists for medical-device manufacturers.
